author: Gaurav Kurhekar
headline: Senior Data Engineer @ Atlas Copco | Azure & Databricks Certified | Guiding Data Enthusiasts & Professionals to Transition into Data Careers by Sharing Practical Data Engineering Knowledge & Best Practices
text:
Hi All,

One of the interview questions which is mostly asked in Data Engineering : 

 How to normalize/Flatten the nested json once you have got the data extracted from upstream application via API integration?
-> Suppose you have got the data extracted from the upstream application via REST API (GET HTTPS METHODS) and it is in json format. 

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟭 : First parse the json to an actual json format using json()
 data = json_data.json()

Now you have nested json like : 
data = [{'name': 'Vidit', 'age': 27, 'address':{'city':'Bengaluru', 'locality':'Electronic_City'}}]

 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟮: Now we can load the data into a Pyspark DataFrame like : 

 from pyspark.sql import functions as f

 df = spark.createDataFrame(data)

 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟯: Use explode() to flatten/normalize the json data into 1-D arrays :

 df1 = df.select(f.explode('address').alias('Address'))

 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟰: Now select the columns out of the address column :

 df1.select([f.col('Address.city').alias('City'), f.col('Address.locality').alias('Locality')]).display()

 This is one of the ways out to flatten/normalize the JSON data in a Pyspark DataFrame. 

 Hope this will help you out!!

headline: Azure Data Engineer • Software Engineer • 59K+ Followers • Data Engineering Influencer & Creator • Helping Data Engineers Crack Interviews • ADF • Databricks • SQL • PySpark • Data Engineering Interview Prep & Courses
text:
Why most Data Engineers fail interviews:-
❌ Great in SQL → weak in Python
❌ Good in Python → weak in PySpark
❌ Know PySpark → zero real-world scenarios
❌ Know scenarios → weak in DSA
❌ Know tools → can’t explain architecture

Here are the 5 skills you MUST master:

1. SQL (Strong foundation):-

Window functions, aggregations, joins.

2. Python (Production mindset):-

Large file handling, data quality, profiling.

3. PySpark (Real performance):-

Shuffle reduction, DAG, partitions, skew fix.

4. DSA (Logical thinking):-

Arrays, hashmaps, sliding window, 2-pointer.

5. Cloud Architecture (Complete understanding):-

Bronze → Silver → Gold
Delta Lake
Pipeline monitoring
Cost optimization

Master these → 15–60 LPA is achievable.
